About Us

Built on unity, service, and accountability.

Our Local is committed to bringing members together so every supervisor has a stronger voice in the workplace. We believe in unity over division, communication over confusion, and action that moves the membership forward.

We work to support fair wages, pay equity, member representation, transparency, safe working conditions, and respect for every member of AFSCME Local 6368.

Unit S MOU Highlight: Labor Management Committees

Member update from the Unit S MOU for AFSCME Local 6368. This section explains how Unit S members serve on Labor Management Committees and confirms that they participate as labor representatives.

Section 3 — Key Language

The Union shall select or appoint its members to the Unit S LMCs.

All parties understand that when Unit S members participate in a Labor Management Committee, they do so as a representative of labor, not management.

  • Departmental/Principal Unit LMCs, in addition to the Chair, shall include at least two (2) and up to three (3) Bargaining Unit S representatives.
  • Upon agreement of the co-chairs, additional Unit S members may be added to the committee when the subjects under discussion warrant.
  • The composition of sub-department LMCs, including the number of Unit S members and management representatives, will be by agreement of the co-chairs of those respective committees.
Local 6368 reminder: Unit S LMC participation is labor representation, not management representation.
